intro: Some official positions of professional institutions on plant-based diets:

items.title: World Health Organization (WHO)
quotes: Diets rich in plant-based foods and with fewer animal source foods are associated with improved health outcomes and a lower risk of many noncommunicable diseases.
Well-planned vegetarian and vegan diets can be nutritionally adequate, but may require attention to specific nutrients.

items.title: Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics and Dietitians of Canada
quotes: Well-planned vegan and other types of vegetarian diets are appropriate for all stages of the life cycle, including during pregnancy, lactation, infancy, childhood, and adolescence. Vegetarian diets offer a number of nutritional benefits, including lower levels of saturated fat, cholesterol, and animal protein as well as higher levels of carbohydrates, fiber, magnesium, potassium, folate, and antioxidants such as vitamins C and E and phytochemicals.

items.title: British Dietetic Association
quotes: Plant-based diets can support healthy living at every age and life stage. But as with any diet, you should plan your plant-based eating to meet your nutritional needs.

Plant-based eating is recognised as an intervention to improve health outcomes. They could reduce your risk of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease and some cancers and may help you manage your weight.

items.title: Ministry of Health Malaysia
quotes: …plant-based diets for all age groups… the dietary guideline prioritises health promotion and disease prevention, promoting the adoption of plant-based diets for all age groups.

items.title: Ministry of Health Israel
quotes: A balanced, healthy and diverse vegetarian or vegan diet can satisfy all our dietary requirements from infancy to old age, while also providing health benefits.
